q: Oxidation and reduction reactions involve the transfer of oxygen atoms, or hydrogen atoms, electrons, or change in ____.
e: Oxidation and reduction reactions involve the transfer of oxygen atoms, or hydrogen atoms, electrons, or change in oxidation numbers. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen (or ____ element) to a substance.
e: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen (or electronegative element) to a substance. Oxidation is loss of electrons, which raises oxidation number.

q: Reduction is the ____ of oxygen (or electronegative element) from a substance.
e: Reduction is the removal of oxygen (or electronegative element) from a substance. Reduction is gain of electrons, which lowers oxidation number.

q: Oxidation is the removal of hydrogen (or ____ element) from a substance.
e: Oxidation is the removal of hydrogen (or electropositive element) from a substance. Oxidation is loss of electrons, which raises oxidation number.

q: Oxidation is the ____ of electrons by an element, compound or ion.
e: Oxidation is the loss of electrons by an element, compound or ion. Oxidation is loss of electrons, which raises oxidation number.

q: Reduction is the ____ of electrons by an element, compound or ion.
e: Reduction is the gain of electrons by an element, compound or ion. Reduction is gain of electrons, which lowers oxidation number.
